newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary agency seeks to publish credit ratings.
newsitem.headline: Hungary agency seeks to publish credit ratings.

text.p: Hungary's first credit rating agency, IHB Rt, asked the state securities watchdog APTF to allow it to prepare public ratings for Hungarian securities issues, the rating agency said on Thursday.

IHB chief executive officer Sandor Body told a news conference that according to the new securities law, which took effect on January 1, APTF should define the principles on the basis of which it regards a credit rating agency as feasible.
"The APTF is just evaluating our methodology and the the company's professional authenticity," Body said.

The APTF decision would enable IHB, which has already prepared confidential ratings for food industry and trading companies, to publish ratings in the official bulletins of public securities offerings, he said.

Hungarian companies are not obliged to enclose a rating to their security issue bulletins, but such a rating could much improve the view clients take of companies, banks, insurance firms and brokerages, Body said.
The news conference was held only days after a panic run on Postabank, Hungary's second largest bank, triggered by rumours about Postabank's liquidity.
"If there were a systematic rating, it would work against rumour-mongering," said IHB Chairman Tamas Bacskai.
IHB's registered capital of 30 million forints is held by Bankconsult Kft and Masped Finance Rt, Body said, adding that IHB planned a capital raise of 50 to 70 million forints this year.
Following the capital increase no one shareholder would have a stake of more than 15 percent, thus guaranteeing the independence essential for the working of a rating agency, Body added.
